content.user_title: Build Molecular ML Workflows with DeepChem
content.value_statement: Molecular modeling projects often need correct featurization, splitting, model choice, and evaluation. This skill guides DeepChem workflows for reliable property prediction, benchmarks, and transfer learning.
actual_capabilities: Explains DeepChem loaders for CSV, SDF, FASTA, image, and JSON molecular data.
Recommends featurizers for fingerprints, descriptors, graph models, sequence models, and transfer learning.
Provides workflows for MoleculeNet datasets such as Tox21, BBBP, Delaney, FreeSolv, and QM datasets.
Guides training and evaluation for scikit-learn models, multitask networks, GCN, GAT, MPNN, AttentiveFP, and pretrained models.
Includes scripts for solubility prediction, graph neural network training, and transfer learning.
limitations: Requires DeepChem and optional model dependencies to be installed in the user environment.
Does not replace experimental validation or expert chemical safety review.
Example workflows may need adaptation for proprietary datasets, hardware limits, and package versions.
Pretrained model availability may depend on external model repositories and local dependencies.

use_cases.title: Screen Candidate Molecules
use_cases.description: Predict solubility, toxicity, and ADMET properties with appropriate featurizers and scaffold-aware validation.

use_cases.title: Benchmark Molecular Models
use_cases.description: Compare baseline, deep learning, and graph neural network models on MoleculeNet datasets with consistent metrics.

use_cases.title: Fine-Tune Pretrained Models
use_cases.description: Adapt ChemBERTa or GROVER style workflows to small chemistry datasets while controlling overfitting.

prompt_templates.title: Run a DeepChem Baseline
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a custom molecular CSV.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me train a simple DeepChem baseline for a CSV with SMILES column {smiles_column} and target {target_column}. Recommend featurization, splitting, metrics, and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Select a Molecular Model
prompt_templates.scenario: Choose a model family before implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: I have {sample_count} molecules for {task_type}. Compare fingerprint, descriptor, graph neural network, and transfer learning options for DeepChem. Explain the tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Build a MoleculeNet Benchmark
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a DeepChem MoleculeNet benchmark for {dataset_name}. Include split strategy, model choices, metrics, expected checks, and how to report results.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Transfer Learning Study
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for small chemistry datasets.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a DeepChem transfer learning study for {property_name} using pretrained molecular models. Include data preparation, fine-tuning settings, validation risks, and comparison baselines.

output_examples.input: I have a small solubility CSV with SMILES and measured logS values.
output_examples.output: Recommended approach: start with circular fingerprints and a random forest baseline, then compare a multitask regressor. Use scaffold splitting and report RMSE, MAE, and R squared on the held-out set.

output_examples.input: I want to compare GCN and AttentiveFP on Tox21.
output_examples.output: Expected plan: load Tox21 with graph features, use scaffold splits, train both models with the same epochs and batch size, and compare ROC-AUC per task and overall mean performance.

output_examples.input: My dataset has fewer than 700 labeled molecules for a binary activity task.
output_examples.output: Suggested direction: keep a fingerprint baseline, use scaffold validation, and test a pretrained model with low learning rate. Watch for overfitting and report uncertainty across repeated splits.

best_practices: Use scaffold splits for molecular datasets to reduce leakage from similar structures.
Start with simple fingerprint baselines before training graph neural networks.
Track metrics, split strategy, transformers, and dependency versions for reproducible results.
anti_patterns: Using random splits for drug discovery claims without scaffold or time-based validation.
Training large graph models on very small datasets before proving a baseline.
Reporting single metrics without confidence intervals, held-out tests, or chemical domain checks.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps users design DeepChem workflows for molecular property prediction, benchmarking, graph models, and transfer learning.

faq.question: Does it install DeepChem automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides installation guidance, but the user controls package installation in their environment.

faq.question: Can it work with custom CSV files?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance covers CSV loading with SMILES columns, target columns, featurizers, and dataset splitting.

faq.question: Which model should I start with?
faq.answer: Start with a fingerprint baseline, then compare deep learning, graph neural networks, or pretrained models when data size supports them.

faq.question: How does it reduce data leakage?
faq.answer: It recommends scaffold splitting for molecular datasets so similar structures are less likely to appear across splits.

faq.question: Can it validate scientific results?
faq.answer: No. It supports workflow design and evaluation, but experimental validation and expert review remain necessary.
